title: How AI could live up to the hype and still leave investors disappointed
excerpt: Moody's said that AI could be end up being a powerful force in the economy, but still lead to more muted stock gains in the coming years.
content_html:
By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

AI hype is often divided into two main schools of thought: AI will be a game changer for businesses, the economy, and investors, or AI will disappoint on some or all of those fronts.

According to Moody's, there's chance for a middle-of-the-road scenario that combines elements of the two. Unfortunately for investors, the base case it sees is for the technology to ultimately reshape businesses but be relatively underwhelming for markets, especially given how the endless hype has already produced enormous returns and sky-high valuations.

"The internet was a game-changing technology that resulted in enormous productivity gains and ultimately generated significant profits," Zandi wrote. "However, investors discounted all this and much more. Stock market valuations—stock prices relative to corporate earnings—surged."

Yet, in the firm's baseline scenario for the AI boom, AI is powerful force in the economy but "stock prices do not rise much, if at all, through the remainder of this year and next," and it sees the coming years for S&P 500 returns as more muted than the boom that helped lift the benchmark index in the earlier era of the AI buildout.

A chart shared by Moody's shows that its base case is for average annual returns to slowly dwindle, predicting 6.2% average annual growth from 2035 to 2030 and 3.8% annual growth from 2030 to 2035.

On a 10-year basis, the comparison is even more stark. The S&P 500 returned 11.7% annually from 2015 to 2025. Moody's predicts the 10-year average gain from 2025 to 2035 will be 5%.

As the economists noted, stock valuations have only reached their current levels a few times, including in the months leading up to the stock market crash of 1929 and leading up to the collapse of the dot-com bubble in the early 2000s.

While today's AI market isn't quite at the same levels the internet mania, it's not far off. By some metrics, the AI frenzy is more pronounced. As Zandi previously highlighted, AI-linked corporate borrowing has eclipsed debt levels of the dot-com era.

If the AI bubble that Zandi and his team are eyeing bursts, it would likely cause consumer spending to plunge, given the wealth effect of high stock prices has led US households to keep spending. This could tip the economy into a recession, Zandi said.

"If the current market trend persists, a stock market bubble seems more likely than not," Zandi wrote. "The final ingredient for a bubble is that nearly all the naysayers capitulate. They have called out the bubble for so long that they are no longer considered credible. Any skepticism is thrown to the side, and the bubble inflates more."

While the economists don't directly say that they see an AI bubble on the verge of bursting, they also note they see some things that could bring the party to an end.

"There are many potential catalysts for the bursting of the AI stock market bubble. Investors might grow impatient and sell their holdings as long-awaited returns from firms' AI bets get pushed further into the future.

Moody's said that history suggests there's reason to be optimistic that AI will be a game changing force for the economy. It compared it to previous technological explosions like the internal combustion engine and the personal computer as examples of major disruptions that still generated substantial gains in income and wealth, while creating new jobs for workers whose roles were made obsolete.

Even if that plays out for AI, though, the economists still see the distinct possibility that many tech stocks are priced too high, leading to a strong likelihood that AI will fail to generate enough of a return for companies to justify high valuations, and even if they meet expectations, it still might not be enough to please Wall Street.

content_html_zh:
作者：Samuel O'Brient 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

人工智能炒作通常分为两种主要思想流派：人工智能将成为企业、经济和投资者的游戏规则改变者，或者人工智能将在部分或全部方面令人失望。

根据穆迪的说法，有可能出现结合两者要素的中间方案。 对于投资者来说不幸的是，它所看到的基本情况是该技术最终会重塑企业，但对市场来说相对平淡，特别是考虑到无休止的炒作已经产生了巨大的回报和天价估值。

赞迪写道：“互联网是一项改变游戏规则的技术，它极大地提高了生产力，并最终产生了可观的利润。” “然而，投资者对这一切以及更多因素都打了折扣。 股票市场估值——股票价格相对于企业盈利——飙升。”

然而，在该公司对人工智能繁荣的基线情景中，人工智能是经济中的强大力量，但“在今年剩余时间和明年，股价即使有上涨，也不会上涨太多”，并且它认为未来几年标准普尔 500 指数的回报将比早期人工智能建设时代帮助提升基准指数的繁荣更加平淡。

穆迪分享的图表显示，其基本情景是平均年回报率缓慢下降，预计2035年至2030年年均回报率将增长6.2%，2030年至2035年年均回报率将增长3.8%。

以 10 年为基础，这种比较更加明显。 从 2015 年到 2025 年，标准普尔 500 指数的年回报率为 11.7%。 穆迪预测2025年至2035年的10年平均涨幅将为5%。

正如经济学家指出的那样，股票估值只达到目前水平几次，包括 1929 年股市崩盘之前的几个月以及 2000 年代初期互联网泡沫破裂之前的几个月。

虽然今天的人工智能市场与互联网热潮的水平还不太一样，但也相差不远了。 从某些指标来看，人工智能的狂热更加明显。 正如赞迪之前强调的那样，与人工智能相关的企业借款已经超过了互联网时代的债务水平。

如果赞迪和他的团队所关注的人工智能泡沫破裂，可能会导致消费者支出大幅下降，因为高股价的财富效应导致美国家庭继续支出。 赞迪说，这可能会使经济陷入衰退。

赞迪写道：“如果当前的市场趋势持续下去，股市泡沫的可能性似乎更大。” “泡沫的最后一个因素是几乎所有反对者都会投降。 他们长期以来一直在呼吁泡沫，以至于他们不再被认为是可信的。 任何怀疑都会被抛到一边，泡沫就会进一步膨胀。”

虽然经济学家没有直接表示他们看到人工智能泡沫即将破裂，但他们也指出，他们看到了一些可能导致泡沫破裂的事情。

“人工智能股市泡沫的破裂有许多潜在的催化剂。 随着企业人工智能投资的期待已久的回报被进一步推迟，投资者可能会变得不耐烦并出售所持股份。

穆迪表示，历史表明，我们有理由乐观地认为人工智能将成为改变经济游戏规则的力量。 它将其与内燃机和个人电脑等之前的技术爆炸进行了比较，作为重大颠覆的例子，这些颠覆仍然带来了收入和财富的大幅增长，同时为那些已经过时的工人创造了新的就业机会。

不过，即使人工智能的情况如此，经济学家仍然认为许多科技股定价过高的可能性很大，导致人工智能很可能无法为公司带来足够的回报来证明高估值的合理性，而且即使它们符合预期，也可能不足以取悦华尔街。
